doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Messengers rehearsal and Blue Note recording routine at Van Gelder's
summary: With Blue Note the band had four days to prepare solos and recorded on the fifth day at Rudy Van Gelder's for minimal fees.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Uh … Let me see. Well, when, when necessary, yeah. It wasn't no rehearsal … uh rehearsal-oriented uh, uh concept uh with the Messengers. We had to rehearse. I mean, for the record date, but with Blue Note you had uh, I mean we had four days to prepare the solos and everything and then on the fifth day you went out to Rudy Van Gelder's and recorded it.
And they paid you for all of that?
Oh yeah. Minimal uh lunch money, yeah, type fees, yeah. But we were glad to get that, goin' to Manhattan and play …
